name: burpsuite
plain: Burp Suite sits between your browser and a website. Every request your browser sends goes through Burp first, so you can read it, stop it, change it and send it again. That is how you test what a web app really does, not just what the page lets you click.

The free Community edition has everything a CTF needs: Proxy (catch and change requests), Repeater (resend one request again and again with edits), Decoder (convert encodings), Comparer (diff two responses) and a slow Intruder (automated guessing). Scanner and Collaborator belong to Burp Pro.

The browser must trust Burp's certificate for HTTPS, and be pointed at Burp's listener, normally 127.0.0.1 port 8080. The built-in browser (Proxy > Intercept > Open browser) is already set up for both.
when: See exactly what a web form sends and what the server answers.
Change a hidden field, cookie, header or parameter and resend.
Brute-force or fuzz a field with a wordlist.
Decode a strange token (Base64, URL, hex).

examples.title: Start the proxy the easy way
examples.explain: The built-in Chromium is pre-configured for the proxy and trusts Burp's CA, so HTTPS works at once. Browse to your lab target in it.

examples.title: Catch and edit a request
examples.cmd: Proxy > Intercept > Intercept is on  >  edit the text  >  Forward
examples.explain: With intercept on, each request waits for you. Change a parameter (price=100 to price=1) in the raw text and press Forward to send it. Turn intercept off to let traffic flow and read it later in HTTP history.

examples.title: Resend a request again and again
examples.cmd:
Right-click a request in HTTP history > Send to Repeater  (Ctrl+R)
In Repeater: edit, then Send  (Ctrl+Space)
examples.explain: Repeater is your lab bench. Change one thing, press Send, read the response on the right, repeat. This is where most testing happens.

examples.title: Guess values with Intruder
examples.cmd: Right-click > Send to Intruder (Ctrl+I) > Positions: select the value, click Add § > Payloads: load a list > Start attack
examples.explain: Intruder replaces the marked position with every payload. Sort the results by Status or Length: the odd one out is usually the hit. Community Intruder is rate-limited.

examples.title: Decode a token
examples.cmd: Decoder tab > paste text > Decode as > Base64 / URL / HTML / Hex
examples.explain: Quickly turn a cookie or parameter into readable text, or encode your payload before sending.

examples.title: Compare two responses
examples.cmd: Right-click a response > Send to Comparer (twice) > Words or Bytes
examples.explain: Highlights the differences between, for example, a logged-in and a logged-out page.

examples.title: Limit Burp to your target
examples.cmd: Target > Site map > right-click the host > Add to scope  (then Proxy > HTTP history > filter: show only in-scope)
examples.explain: Scope keeps the history readable and prevents you from testing things that are not yours.

examples.title: Save a request for sqlmap
examples.cmd: Right-click a request > Copy to file  >  sqlmap -r request.txt
examples.explain: Saves the raw request with cookies and body so sqlmap can reuse it.

examples.title: Replace a response before the browser sees it
examples.cmd: Proxy > Proxy settings > Match and replace
examples.explain: Rules that rewrite headers or bodies automatically, such as changing 'isAdmin=false' to 'isAdmin=true' in responses.

mistakes: Leaving intercept on and thinking the browser is broken: pages hang because Burp is waiting for Forward.
Testing out-of-scope hosts: set scope and filter the history.
Forgetting to import the CA certificate in an outside browser: you get certificate warnings.
Pointing Intruder at a real production site: Intruder is noisy.
Editing the request and breaking Content-Length: Burp usually fixes it for you, but check when a request fails.
Using Burp where the event bans proxy tools: read the rules.
